design.approval_target: existing governance target evolution_proposal; no new target, no second approval store
design.binding: tenant_id + target_id/proposal_id=program_id + target_version/proposal_revision=post-submit program revision + proposal_content_digest over source_decision_ids and each linked decision's immutable content fingerprint
design.who_files_the_request: the BFF, with the operator's own credential, under deterministic id apv-program-{program_id}-r{revision} (resubmission reuses it; it is in the approvals queue read by GET /bff/approvals). Binding is computed by the Evolution owner (GET /api/evolution/programs/{id}/approval-binding).
design.who_verifies: the Evolution owner, through ApprovalReader via EVOLUTION_GOVERNANCE_BASE_URL; unset means HTTP 503 (fail closed), never skipped
design.execution_gate: dispatch_outbox.require_execution_approval additionally accepts the human approval of an ACTIVE program that lists the decision and whose digest covers its immutable content; per-decision evolution_execute grants still work unchanged
design.run_linking: dispatch_worker POSTs /api/evolution/proposals/{id}/dispatch-run after submit; the owner reads the run back from its plane and checks tenant/decision before linking. GET /api/evolution/programs/{id}/runs re-reads each run; success only from a terminal receipt, failed/rejected stay failed, unreadable is unknown
design.bff_approve_program_catalog: requires_approval changed True -> False: the owner is the single gate and reads the program's own governance approval; keeping True would require a second, separate approval id for the same human decision

stub_finding.what_a_dispatched_run_executes: ResearchPlaneAdapter._ensure_run omits adapter, so research DispatchRunBody defaults adapter/requested_mode/dispatch_mode to 'stub' and the run is created with status 'queued' and summary 'Stub research orchestration run queued...'. The stub label itself performs nothing. The only real work is the side effect services/research/main.py:dispatch_run triggers when parameters carry decision_id and target_artifact_id: _trigger_retrain_execution, which creates a training session, reads the artifact from the registry, mutates it to a new candidate version and only then sets the run 'completed' (any exception sets 'failed'). A run is therefore 'completed' only after that real sequence, and the dispatch receipt maps completed->succeeded only from the orchestrator's own readback.
stub_finding.gap_fixed: _trigger_retrain_execution fired for ANY action_type carrying those two parameters, i.e. a revalidate/freeze/revive decision would have been run as a retrain mutation. It is now gated to action_type == 'retrain' (absent action_type keeps legacy behaviour). Other action types stay 'queued' and so never converge to executed: they are not reported complete for work that was not done.
stub_finding.not_reported_as_evolution: a stub-labelled queued run is never presented as a completed evolution; BFF/owner runs read reports it as running/unknown

conflict_resolved.qualify_r2_sweep_submit: EVOLUTION-PROGRAM-QUALIFY-R2 has the daily-sweep identity submit its program for review. It has no human credential and cannot file the Governance request. Resolution: the owner lets ONLY evolution-daily-sweep on an auto_qualified draft submit without an approval id (review.approval_id=null, program under_review, nothing approvable); a human submit then files and attaches the request (system identities can never attach). Approve is refused with approval_missing until then. No R2 test assertion was changed.
